articles.title: Free AI website design prompts: learn the structure by copying a finished one
articles.excerpt: Most advice about AI website design prompts is abstract: "be specific", "describe the style", "give it constraints". It's all true, and it's still hard to act on. The fastest way I know to get better…
articles.body: Most advice about AI website design prompts is abstract: "be specific", "describe the style", "give it constraints". It's all true, and it's still hard to act on. The fastest way I know to get better at writing prompts for Lovable, Bolt, Cursor or Claude is to take a prompt that already produced a good-looking page, run it, and then take it apart. This post walks through that exercise using free prompts, so you can do it today without paying for anything. Where to get a finished prompt MotionSites keeps a free shelf at motionsites.org/free . These are design directions you can copy without a paid plan. At the time of writing it mixes two kinds of things: Full hero or site directions , for example a travel hero with a morphing dropdown and a hero built around a refracting glass cube.

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built On 4 October my AI coach, an agent I run in OpenClaw, had planned a long ride in Zone 2: heart rate under 140, even on the climbs. A bit more than two hours in, the climb to Canareccia turned up to 11 % for 900 metres. I was in 34×34, the easiest gear on the bike, my legs turning at 57 rpm. My heart was at 170. After my long rides, the coach keeps saying the same thing: my Zone 2 rides drift into tempo. Its notes even have a theory: I chase personal records on Strava segments. That Sunday I beat my best time up Canareccia by one second, so I won't argue with that one.

articles.title: Kustomize patch env variable with valueFrom in a Helm chart
articles.excerpt: Many charts take extra environment variables as a map of names to values name and value. A variable that comes from a valueFrom, which such a map helm template, then with Kapitan's mutate generator. T…
articles.body: Many charts take extra environment variables as a map of names to values and render each entry as name and value . A variable that comes from a Secret, a ConfigMap or the downward API needs valueFrom , which such a map cannot express. This post adds those entries to the rendered Deployments instead, merged into the container by its name, first with a Kustomize strategic merge patch over helm template , then with Kapitan 's mutate generator . The two cases come from open issues against the KEDA HTTP add-on chart and the Crossplane chart. Each patch was rendered from the chart version named in its section with Helm 4.3.1, Kustomize 5.8.3, and Kapitan 0.36.3 with mutate 0.1.0, and the result was installed on a kind cluster on Kubernetes 1.37.0.

articles.title: Detecting exploitation of the Plex timeline SSRF in server and network telemetry
articles.excerpt: Detecting exploitation of the Plex timeline SSRF in server and network telemetry Patching CVE-2026-96652 closes the path that lets a caller force Plex Media Server to issue an outbound POST. Between t…
articles.body: Detecting exploitation of the Plex timeline SSRF in server and network telemetry Patching CVE-2026-96652 closes the path that lets a caller force Plex Media Server to issue an outbound POST. Between the advisory and the upgrade there is a window where detection is the only control available. The flaw's mechanics show where to look. First a request to one media endpoint, then an HTTP request leaving the server towards an address with nothing to do with the library. Vulnerability overview The CNA record states that Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10861 allows SSRF via /player/timeline and that an attacker using any X-Plex-Token value can place a full URL in the protocol parameter. CVSS v3.1 is 4.3 with AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N , CVSS v4.0 is 5.3, and the weakness is CWE-918.

articles.body: The October full moon rises tonight! Here's everything you need to know about the "Hunter's Moon," including where to see it, how it got its name and other tricks of the light and mind that could conspire to create a truly spectacular lunar light show. October's moon reaches 100% illumination at 12:12 a.m. EDT (0412 GMT) on Oct. 26, as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. The shadowy terminator that separates the day and night side of the moon is conspicuously absent around this time, as are the shadows that throw craters into spectacular relief during the waxing and waning lunar phases.

Samsung flipped the script and became known for reliable software with timely updates. One UI 9 running Android 17 is undoubtedly another solid software update. It’s been a smooth experience so far on my Galaxy S26 Plus , and Samsung’s been spot-on with patches. articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

articles.title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks
articles.excerpt: The fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was one giant gimmick: shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.
articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

articles.title: Medusa's eye, Halloween fireballs and more: 5 skywatching targets to look out for this spooky season
articles.excerpt: Five spooky skywatching targets perfect for naked eye stargazing this Halloween!
articles.body: The spooky season is officially here! To celebrate, we've put together a list of five Halloween-themed skywatching targets that you can enjoy with nothing but the naked eye or binoculars and, of course, clear skies. Over millennia, the night sky has helped shape human beliefs. In return, we have imprinted our myths, stories and perceptions upon it, seeing monsters and mythology in the twinkling lights of the stars and assigning sinister aspects to innocent cosmic objects. Many of these ghostly impressions and meanings have survived to the present day. Here are a few of our favorites. The Pleiades open star cluster Don't be fooled by their beauty; the blue-white stars of the Pleiades are dripping in spooky lore.
